definition: Inexorable means impossible to persuade or hold back; deaf to every plea, appeal, or delay.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word inexorable. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know inexorable should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The tide was inexorable; the children's seawall of sand, engineered all afternoon, was gone in four unhurried waves.
Firm is far weaker than inexorable: a firm official holds the line today but can still be brought around by a strong enough case, while inexorable means no case will ever be strong enough.

Adamant is strong but still one rung below inexorable: an adamant refusal announces that persuasion is unwelcome, while inexorable means persuasion is impossible — the tide does not attend the hearing.

Relentless measures pressure that never lets up — relentless rain, a relentless interviewer — and it says nothing about persuasion, because nobody argues with rain. Inexorable adds the shut door: appeals were possible, appeals were made, and appeals moved nothing.

Unyielding describes the stance: a person or position that will not bend under pressure. Inexorable describes the outcome of every possible approach — not just firm against force, but deaf to pleading, unmoved by the best case anyone can make.
